sources.shortSummary: The unit distinguishes primary, foreign, unique, CHECK, DEFAULT and NOT NULL constraints, and describes table-independent sequence allocation and range reservation.

sources.shortSummary: The unit separates typed relational columns from variable JSON attributes, demonstrates indexed computed scalar projections, and explicitly calls JSON_MODIFY for JSON text updates.

sources.shortSummary: Repository-wide .github/copilot-instructions.md provides automatic guidance; .prompt.md files hold reusable invoked tasks. Guidance is versioned context, not an authorization mechanism.

sources.title: Unique constraints and check constraints
sources.shortSummary: UNIQUE applies to the specified column tuple and permits NULL under its documented uniqueness rule; CHECK rejects FALSE rather than UNKNOWN and enforces row-level predicates.

sources.title: Sequence numbers
sources.shortSummary: Sequences allocate independently of transactions and tables; unused or rolled-back allocations can leave gaps. Repeated references to the same sequence within one statement share a value per output row.

sources.title: Create views
sources.shortSummary: Ordinary views store a SELECT definition rather than a reusable materialized intermediate rowset. The unit introduces explicit projection and writable-view CHECK OPTION.

sources.title: CREATE VIEW (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: CREATE VIEW distinguishes dependency protection through SCHEMABINDING, post-update visibility through CHECK OPTION, definition obfuscation and browse-mode metadata. CHECK OPTION does not constrain direct base-table updates.

sources.title: Create triggers
sources.shortSummary: DML triggers react to statements, using inserted/deleted rowsets for new/old values. AFTER and INSTEAD OF triggers have distinct positions in the modification workflow.

sources.title: CREATE TRIGGER (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: CREATE TRIGGER specifies old/new logical rowsets, statement activation, constraint order and view restrictions: constraints precede AFTER, while INSTEAD OF replaces the requested operation.

sources.title: Organize queries with common table expressions
sources.shortSummary: CTEs organize one statement's transformations; recursive CTEs combine an anchor with recursive steps and need a genuine termination condition.

sources.title: WITH common_table_expression (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: A CTE is statement-scoped and not an explicitly materialized reusable cache. Recursive member columns must match anchor types; recursion continues until no rows, independently of an outer filter.

sources.title: Apply window functions for analytics
sources.shortSummary: Window functions preserve row detail while applying partition, logical order and frame semantics. Ranking functions differ in tie handling; LAG/LEAD and FIRST_VALUE/LAST_VALUE access ordered values.

sources.title: SELECT - OVER clause (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: OVER separates partition membership, ordering and row/range boundaries. RANGE CURRENT ROW includes ordering peers; ROWS uses physical ordered positions, and frame defaults apply only to functions accepting frames.

sources.title: Process JSON data with built-in functions
sources.shortSummary: Credential-linked instruction names JSON_VALUE, JSON_QUERY, OPENJSON, JSON_OBJECT and JSON_ARRAYAGG, with scalar/fragment extraction, explicit rowset projection, constructors and computed scalar indexes.

sources.title: JSON_VALUE (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: JSON_VALUE without RETURNING extracts nvarchar(4000) scalar text; overlength values yield NULL in lax mode and errors in strict mode. Object/array paths need a fragment-oriented API.

sources.title: OPENJSON (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: OPENJSON exposes default key/value/type rows or an explicit WITH schema. Property matching is BIN2/case-sensitive, literal dotted output names are not nested paths, and AS JSON requires nvarchar(max) for fragments.

sources.title: JSON_QUERY (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: JSON_QUERY returns an object/array fragment as nvarchar(max), defaults to the root path, and returns NULL for a scalar in lax mode. Proper fragments are not re-escaped by JSON output functions.

sources.title: JSON_MODIFY (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: JSON_MODIFY returns changed JSON text: append extends an existing array, ordinary paths update addressed values, strict SQL NULL retains an existing key as JSON null, and lax SQL NULL deletes it.

sources.title: JSON_OBJECT (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: JSON_OBJECT constructs key/value objects, defaults to NULL ON NULL, and uses ABSENT ON NULL to omit SQL-NULL-valued keys rather than numeric zero or empty strings.

sources.title: JSON_ARRAYAGG (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: JSON_ARRAYAGG orders elements through its internal ORDER BY and defaults to ABSENT ON NULL; NULL ON NULL preserves positional null slots. Current syntax includes an optional native-json return.

sources.title: Build effective tables
sources.shortSummary: Table design balances exact numeric types, bounded columns, integrity and workload-specific indexing; the unit explicitly discusses DECIMAL precision and storage.

sources.title: Optimize with indexes
sources.shortSummary: The unit distinguishes base rowstore/clustered columnstore organization from secondary nonclustered columnstore for operational analytics while retaining transactional access paths.

sources.title: Use specialized table types
sources.shortSummary: Specialized table choices include memory-optimized, temporal, external, ledger and graph tables, with links to their dedicated creation and architecture contracts.

sources.title: Partition tables for scale
sources.shortSummary: Partitioning uses a function for boundaries, a scheme for storage placement and suitable aligned indexes for maintenance. The unit names ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION for splits and merges.

sources.title: Create stored procedures
sources.shortSummary: Stored procedures encapsulate parameterized server-side operations, can return results and output values, and use NOCOUNT to reduce affected-row messages rather than remove result sets.

sources.title: Create scalar functions
sources.shortSummary: Scalar functions return one typed value and centralize expression logic. The unit discusses determinism, side effects and explicit date inputs and links CREATE FUNCTION.

sources.title: Create table-valued functions
sources.shortSummary: TVFs expose parameterized rowsets: inline functions use one SELECT and multistatement functions build a declared return table. APPLY supplies row-dependent arguments from a left table source.

sources.title: JSON data in SQL Server
sources.shortSummary: SQL supports mixed relational and JSON columns and explicit text mutation of array elements. The current overview marks native json and several SQL Server 2025 JSON extensions generally available.

sources.title: Match patterns with regular expressions
sources.shortSummary: The advanced SQL unit names regex filtering, replacement, extraction, position, count, matching and splitting functions and links the dedicated regular-expression overview.

sources.title: Find approximate matches with fuzzy string functions
sources.shortSummary: The linked unit introduces distance versus normalized similarity and using candidate filters before approximate matching; exact current algorithm and lifecycle are delegated to product references.

sources.title: Compare rows with correlated subqueries
sources.shortSummary: Correlated subqueries express row-dependent existence and comparisons. EXISTS tests whether a row is present, while aggregates and anti-existence require attention to NULL and empty input.

sources.title: Handle errors with TRY...CATCH
sources.shortSummary: The error-handling unit introduces TRY...CATCH, ERROR_* metadata, THROW, transaction cleanup and nested procedure propagation with links to exact statement contracts.

sources.title: Enable GitHub Copilot and Fabric Copilot
sources.shortSummary: Enabling AI-assisted SQL development involves the correct host components and Copilot account, or Fabric tenant/capacity/workspace prerequisites rather than database permissions alone.

sources.shortSummary: Model selection and MCP tool configuration are separate: Agent mode, registered servers and enabled tools supply live context, while a model choice determines the responding model.

sources.title: decimal and numeric (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: DECIMAL precision counts total digits and scale counts fractional digits; integral capacity is p-s. Precision 1–9 uses five bytes, 10–19 nine bytes, and narrowing scale can round values.

sources.title: CREATE COLUMNSTORE INDEX (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: A nonclustered columnstore can retain rowstore base organization, select supported columns and filter rows. Its SQL Server 2022 syntax differs from clustered conversion and excludes INCLUDE and nvarchar(max) columns.

sources.title: Create a system-versioned temporal table
sources.shortSummary: The current creation article requires temporal history to match current-table column count, names, order and types. History cannot have a primary key or unique index. Skipping temporal data consistency checks does not waive those schema requirements.

sources.title: Primary and foreign key constraints
sources.shortSummary: Foreign keys enforce referenced-row integrity and distinguish NO ACTION, CASCADE, SET NULL and SET DEFAULT. SET DEFAULT still produces values that must satisfy the foreign key; defaults are not exemptions.

sources.title: ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION atomically changes every dependent table/index. All using schemes need NEXT USED for a split; merging removes a boundary but preserves and combines rows.

sources.title: CREATE FUNCTION (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: CREATE FUNCTION distinguishes scalar, inline-table and multistatement-table forms, function options, local-state restrictions and determinism/data-access requirements for indexed computed columns.

sources.title: User-defined functions
sources.shortSummary: User-defined functions compose reusable scalar or rowset results without persistent side effects. Function errors can cancel the invoking statement; TRY...CATCH is not allowed inside a T-SQL UDF.

sources.title: ALTER FUNCTION (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: ALTER FUNCTION can replace a definition within its existing function kind, but cannot change scalar to table-valued, inline to multistatement, or T-SQL to CLR forms.

sources.title: FROM clause plus JOIN, APPLY, PIVOT (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: FROM defines joins and lateral APPLY: the right table source can receive left-row values, CROSS APPLY drops an empty right rowset, and OUTER APPLY preserves the left row.

sources.title: SET NOCOUNT (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: SET NOCOUNT ON suppresses affected-row/DONEINPROC messages while @@ROWCOUNT still updates and explicit SELECT result sets remain available.

sources.title: sp_executesql (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: sp_executesql compiles a separate dynamic batch and binds data values through declared typed parameters; caller variables are not implicitly visible and concatenation is not made safe by the procedure name.

sources.title: TRY...CATCH (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: TRY...CATCH handles appropriate execution errors and lower-scope compilation errors, but not same-level compilation failures. An XACT_STATE of -1 permits reads or full rollback, not writes or commit.

sources.title: Regular expressions
sources.shortSummary: Current SQL regex uses RE2-based syntax with documented character classes, groups and flags. Regex matching is independent of SQL linguistic collation and has platform and input-size bounds.

sources.title: REGEXP_REPLACE (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: REGEXP_REPLACE uses backslash-number replacement groups, one-based start and an occurrence argument whose zero default replaces all matches; unmatched strings are retained.

sources.title: REGEXP_SUBSTR (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: REGEXP_SUBSTR selects a match occurrence, optional capture group and explicit flags from a one-based starting position; no match returns NULL.

sources.title: EDIT_DISTANCE (Transact-SQL) preview
sources.shortSummary: Preview EDIT_DISTANCE uses the current Damerau-Levenshtein Optimal String Alignment contract. A nonnegative maximum returns exact distances within the bound and maximum+1 for greater distances.

sources.title: EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY (Transact-SQL) preview
sources.shortSummary: Preview EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY normalizes edit distance by maximum string length to an integer score from 0 to 100, where higher means more similar.

sources.title: Subqueries (SQL Server)
sources.shortSummary: Correlated subqueries bind outer values explicitly; EXISTS tests returned row presence. Unqualified missing inner columns can silently bind to an outer scope.

sources.title: EXISTS (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: EXISTS is true for any returned row, regardless of its projected value; NOT EXISTS is true only when the correlated subquery returns no rows.

sources.title: COUNT (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: COUNT(*) without GROUP BY produces a cardinality value, including zero for empty input, whereas grouped counts return rows per existing group. COUNT(expression) ignores NULL expressions.

sources.title: Enable and configure Copilot in Microsoft Fabric
sources.shortSummary: Fabric Copilot enablement combines eligible paid capacity, supported region, tenant settings, any delegated capacity settings, workspace placement and scoped user access.

sources.title: LAG (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: LAG returns a value from a preceding row in its ordered partition, using a default only when the offset falls outside that partition. Partition and output filtering must preserve intended history.

sources.title: SELECT (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: SELECT's logical binding order evaluates WHERE before SELECT expressions. A CTE or derived query can compute window results over one rowset and apply a report filter at a later query level.

sources.title: Always Encrypted
sources.shortSummary: Without enclaves, deterministic encryption supports equality operations while randomized encryption does not support searching; client drivers encrypt parameters and keys remain outside the engine in plaintext form.

sources.title: Encrypt a Column of Data
sources.shortSummary: Shows AES symmetric keys protected by certificates, binary ciphertext storage, and opening the key before SQL encryption/decryption, with optional matching authenticators.

sources.title: Dynamic data masking
sources.shortSummary: SELECT and UNMASK have separate roles; SQL Server 2022 supports column-scoped UNMASK. Output masking leaves underlying values intact, and masked SELECT INTO/export output can become statically masked copies.

sources.title: Row-level security
sources.shortSummary: Separates FILTER and operation-specific BLOCK predicates and explains how policy SCHEMABINDING controls permission checks on predicate functions and lookup tables.

sources.title: GRANT (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: Defines WITH GRANT OPTION and shows a role member using AS role to delegate that role's grant option; AS records the grantor rather than generally granting impersonation.

sources.title: Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure SQL

sources.title: Create and manage external models in SQL
sources.shortSummary: For remote inference, an external model is a reusable database object referencing an endpoint rather than a model trained or hosted by that definition. CREATE registers metadata, ALTER changes it, and AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS invokes a referenced model.

sources.title: Design embeddings for SQL database workloads
sources.shortSummary: Embedding input should carry the meaning required by the retrieval task, while chunk design balances context, semantic focus and model limits. Source IDs, operational fields and numeric values are not categorically forbidden when a task makes them meaningful.

sources.title: Generate and maintain embeddings for SQL database workloads
sources.shortSummary: Embedding refresh must be coordinated with source changes. The admitted SQL Server maintenance comparisons distinguish trigger write-path work, Change Tracking changed-row signals, CDC detailed changes and asynchronous consumers; model hosting alone is not change detection.

sources.shortSummary: The models-module summary directly links the Vector data type and CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL product references. It is retained as an ancestry record rather than executable-feature evidence.

sources.title: Choose an intelligent search approach
sources.shortSummary: Lexical retrieval addresses words and phrases, semantic retrieval addresses meaning expressed with different wording, and hybrid retrieval combines ranked lists. Selection depends on query intent and measured workload tradeoffs.

sources.title: Implement full-text search
sources.shortSummary: SQL full-text search uses a populated full-text index and language-aware predicates or table-valued functions. CONTAINS controls words, phrases, prefixes, inflections and proximity; CONTAINSTABLE returns a key and relevance rank.

sources.title: Prepare SQL for vector search
sources.shortSummary: Vector preparation includes dimensions, storage, metric choice and exact-versus-approximate tradeoffs. Its CREATE VECTOR INDEX example identifies DiskANN; its explicit Preview warning and older index examples must be read alongside current version-specific product references.

sources.title: Implement vector search query patterns
sources.shortSummary: The admitted exact-query scope uses a query embedding from the same model, computes VECTOR_DISTANCE and orders smaller distances first. The unit explicitly names VECTOR_NORMALIZE and VECTORPROPERTY for scale and dimension inspection.

sources.title: Implement hybrid search and ranking
sources.shortSummary: For an exact-vector SQL hybrid implementation, convert each source's relevance ordering into rank positions, combine candidate IDs and sum fractional RRF contributions. Evaluate candidate budgets, weights and relevance metrics on labeled queries.

sources.shortSummary: The search summary's Additional reading links the exact Full-Text Search, Vector data type, VECTOR_DISTANCE and VECTOR_SEARCH documentation pages.

sources.title: Identify RAG use cases and architecture
sources.shortSummary: RAG retrieves request-relevant records, supplies them as prompt context and asks a model to generate a response. It is suitable for changing domain knowledge and traceable source context without treating retraining as the retrieval mechanism.

sources.title: Prepare retrieval context for augmentation
sources.shortSummary: FOR JSON shapes retrieved SQL rows into labeled context. PATH, ROOT, INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES and WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER address different shape requirements; include task-relevant fields and budget the resulting context.

sources.title: Generate and process RAG responses
sources.shortSummary: sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint sends a prepared payload and returns an HTTP envelope around a provider result. The supplied chat-example answer is a scalar at result.choices[0].message.content; JSON_VALUE and JSON_QUERY have distinct extraction roles.

sources.shortSummary: The RAG module's Learn more list directly links the REST stored-procedure reference and FOR JSON product article, completing the required immediate training-to-documentation ancestry.

sources.title: AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: The remote AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS operation references a configured EMBEDDINGS model and sends source text to its endpoint. Request parameters depend on the provider; documented XEvents expose model/request status and errors for diagnosis.

sources.title: AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS requires compatibility level at least 170. FIXED sizes are character counts, optional overlap is an integer percentage from 0 through 50, and output rows include chunk text and within-source order.

sources.title: Vector data type
sources.shortSummary: The selected native float32 vector contract uses fixed dimensions, four-byte components, optimized binary storage and JSON interoperability. The maximum documented dimensions are 1998; Preview float16 and its transport restrictions are separate.

sources.title: VECTOR_DISTANCE (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: VECTOR_DISTANCE computes exact scalar float distances and never uses a vector index. Supported metrics are cosine, Euclidean and negative dot product; lower returned distances sort toward closer results.

sources.title: VECTOR_NORMALIZE (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: VECTOR_NORMALIZE preserves direction while scaling a vector to unit length for norm1, norm2 or norminf. The norms use absolute-value sum, Euclidean length and maximum absolute component respectively.

sources.title: VECTOR_SEARCH (Transact-SQL) (Preview)
sources.shortSummary: VECTOR_SEARCH is Preview and version-specific. Earlier indexes use TOP_N and post-filtering; latest Azure indexes use TOP WITH APPROXIMATE, iterative filtering and optimizer-selected ANN or kNN, with distance-only ascending ordering in the approximate query layer.

sources.title: VECTORPROPERTY (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: VECTORPROPERTY reads Dimensions as an integer and BaseType as a type name. It inspects a supplied vector rather than changing its components or generating a new embedding.

sources.title: CREATE VECTOR INDEX (Transact-SQL) (Preview)
sources.shortSummary: Current Preview vector indexes support DiskANN with cosine, Euclidean or dot metrics. Latest Azure formats require a clustered primary key and at least 100 nonnull vectors at creation, support DML maintenance and require drop/recreate for older-format migration.

sources.title: CONTAINSTABLE (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: CONTAINSTABLE searches a full-text-indexed table and returns KEY plus relevance RANK. Its grammar supports phrases, inflections, proximity and combinations; the result key joins to the table's full-text unique key.

sources.title: Format query results as JSON with FOR JSON
sources.shortSummary: FOR JSON PATH supports dotted alias nesting; output is an array by default. ROOT adds a named wrapper, INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES preserves null properties and WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER is appropriate for a single-row object.

sources.title: JSON_VALUE (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: JSON_VALUE extracts a scalar from nvarchar JSON text. Without RETURNING it yields nvarchar(4000); lax-mode object/array or overlength extraction does not produce the requested scalar.

sources.title: JSON_QUERY (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: JSON_QUERY extracts an object/array JSON fragment, returning nvarchar(max), and allows already-valid JSON fragments to be embedded in FOR JSON output without double escaping.

sources.title: OPENJSON (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: OPENJSON parses JSON text into rows and supports explicit typed WITH projections, property paths and AS JSON fragments. Current questions use Azure SQL Database compatibility level 170 and an explicitly supplied response shape.

sources.title: TOP (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: TOP without a query-level ORDER BY selects an undefined subset. The order controlling a ranked function or an outer UNION result does not by itself bind an inner TOP candidate pool.

sources.title: RANK (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: RANK computes positions using an OVER ordering and returns bigint; query-level ordering separately determines returned row order. Full-text relevance values must be converted to positions for RRF.

sources.title: / (Division) (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: T-SQL integer division truncates the fractional part; result type follows operand precedence. An RRF numerator must participate in noninteger division before evaluation, not be cast after an integer quotient has already become zero.

sources.title: UPDATE (Transact-SQL)
sources.shortSummary: UPDATE changes existing rows satisfying its WHERE search condition and can assign an embedding plus its source-revision marker together. A stipulated application revision enables a guarded persistence step after asynchronous generation.
